clue.text: Bow before convulsion in the North

parts.note: a bow is a curve, an arc
a tic is an involuntary twitch or convulsion

explanation.surface: An archer's bow goes into a spasm somewhere up north.
explanation.definitionFit: Arctic describes the polar region at the far north of the globe, so it serves as an adjective for northern lands.

clue.text: Three boys: one in a hundred at club

parts.note: Roy is a boy's name
Alan is a boy's name
Dan is a boy's name

indicators.note: in tells us the numeral for one is placed inside the word for a hundred

parts.note: a cent is a hundredth part, from Latin centum, a hundred
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Three lads, one in every hundred, gather at the clubhouse.
explanation.walkthrough: The Royal and Ancient Golf Club of St Andrews in Scotland is the historic home of golf and its rule-making body, so 'club' is a golf club in this golf-themed puzzle.
explanation.definitionFit: The Royal and Ancient is the famous golfing institution at St Andrews, a club in the society sense.

clue.text: Something hit it — an iceberg?

indicators.note: something of the following words means part of them, so the answer lies within the run of letters

explanation.surface: A question about what an iceberg struck, or what struck it.
explanation.walkthrough: The ship lies across 'hiT IT AN ICeberg'; the whole clue also describes the liner's fate, as the iceberg was the something it hit.
explanation.definitionFit: The White Star liner famously sank in 1912 after striking an iceberg on its maiden voyage.

clue.text: Store charge here for top performer without one

parts.note: a cap is a top or lid

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside: the performer's letters surround the numeral

parts.note: an actor is a performer
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Where a star performer charges, minus one.
explanation.definitionFit: An electrical component that stores electric charge between two plates is exactly this device.

clue.text: Spirit — don't say it — sleeps (say it)

indicators.note: the bracketed say it tells us to speak the preceding pieces out loud

parts.note: shh is the call to keep quiet, telling someone not to say it, and naps are short sleeps

explanation.surface: A drinker is urged to hush about a spirit that makes one doze.
explanation.definitionFit: Schnapps is a strong distilled liquor, a spirit in the drinks sense.

clue.text: Albatross may be cooked — braised?

indicators.note: cooked suggests the letters are doctored or rearranged, so the next word is mixed up

explanation.surface: Asking whether an albatross might be braised for dinner.
explanation.definitionFit: The albatross is an example of an ocean-going bird, the classic wanderer of the southern seas.

clue.text: Setter debtor? Quick pull up required

annotationWithheld.why: Setter debtor? Quick pull up required (5): HOICK is I (setter) in HOCK (debt), but 'debtor' both supplies HOCK and signals the insertion, one word doing two jobs
annotationWithheld.clue: Setter debtor? Quick pull up required

clue.text: Oppo of Caesar, J., or the opposite

parts.note: Caesar's colleague Mark Antony, written in the same surname-first index style as 'Caesar, J.', with his initial after a comma

explanation.surface: Who was Julius Caesar's sidekick, or his opponent?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Oppo' is British slang for a colleague or mate. Listing Caesar as 'Caesar, J.' prompts Mark Antony in the same register style: Antony, M.
explanation.definitionFit: A word of contrary meaning to another is called by this term, so it names the linguistic opposite.

clue.text: Perfect hours, or a result good for clubs as usual

indicators.note: a result here is what the jumbled letters turn into, so the words before it are rearranged

explanation.surface: Perfect hours on the golf course give a score that clubs think normal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'good for clubs' adds the golf sense: par is the expected score on a hole, so the phrase also means a golfing standard.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means what is normal or to be expected, taken from golf's standard score.

clue.text: Days off without helmet will be hell

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the jumbled letters go round the helmet
off means awry, so the letters of the word before it are jumbled

parts.note: a topi is a sun helmet, a pith helmet

explanation.surface: Days off with no protective headgear will be torment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' is used in its old sense of outside, not lacking; TOPI is a pith helmet worn in India.
explanation.definitionFit: A dystopia is an imagined society of misery and oppression, the opposite of utopia, so a kind of hell.

clue.text: Doctor's American — don't let him out

explanation.surface: An American medic who must be kept confined.
explanation.definitionFit: A junior hospital doctor in the US has this title, and the verb means to confine someone, as in wartime.

clue.text: Club better the 8 in the Highlands

definitions.text: Club better the 8 in the Highlands

parts.words: Club better the 8 in the Highlands
parts.note: a Scottish golf club whose name also suggests a valley plus scores better than par, the expected standard

explanation.surface: A golfer beats the usual score at a Scottish course.
explanation.walkthrough: The 8 is 8 down, a phrase about par; eagles are scores two under par, and a glen is a Highland valley, so the club is the famous Perthshire golf resort.
explanation.definitionFit: A famous golf resort and club in Perthshire, Scotland, venue of the Ryder Cup.

clue.text: Enter rustic to ponce about with unknown complaint

indicators.note: enter means go into, so the rustic's letters go inside the jumbled word
about means around in disorder, so the letters of ponce are rearranged

parts.note: a hick is a country bumpkin, a rustic
x is the algebraic unknown

explanation.surface: A country fellow is told to strut about with something mysterious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ponce about' reads as one idle phrase, but 'about' is the anagram signal and 'Enter' says where the rustic goes.
explanation.definitionFit: Chickenpox is a common childhood illness, and complaint is a familiar word for an ailment.

clue.text: 1 traveller maybe acts on fancy

indicators.note: fancy as a verb hints at imaginative reworking, so the preceding letters are freely rearranged

explanation.surface: A traveller in the far north behaves on a whim.
explanation.walkthrough: '1' points to 1 across, ARCTIC: a tracked snow vehicle travels the polar regions.
explanation.definitionFit: A snowcat is a tracked vehicle for snow, an example of a polar mode of travel.

clue.text: Take 10% off friend after first of month

indicators.note: after places the friend second, following the date that comes first in the answer

parts.note: Dec. I, the first of December, written with the Roman numeral
mate means friend

explanation.surface: A tenth is deducted from a friend's pay at the start of the month.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first of month' is Dec. 1, the first of December, with the Roman numeral I. 'Take 10% off' is the original Roman sense of killing one in ten.
explanation.definitionFit: The Roman army punished mutinous units by killing one soldier in ten, the original sense of this verb.

clue.text: Model in French coast has fruit in theatre

indicators.note: in puts the model inside the French word for coast

parts.note: cote is French for coast, as in Cote d'Azur
the Model T was Ford's famous car
a sloe is the fruit of the blackthorn

explanation.surface: A fashion model on the French Riviera eats fruit in a playhouse.
explanation.walkthrough: The Cottesloe was one of the three auditoria of the National Theatre on London's South Bank (now the Dorfman).
explanation.definitionFit: The smallest stage of the National Theatre in London bore this name for decades.

clue.text: Was one of ancient 25 as result of wearing T-shirt

explanation.surface: A soldier of old and a summer dresser share a look.
explanation.walkthrough: 25 is 25 across, SOLDIERY. 'Bare' is an archaic past tense of 'bear', so a soldier of old 'bare arms'.
explanation.definitionFit: To bear arms is to serve as a soldier, written with the archaic past tense; a short-sleeved top leaves the limbs uncovered.

clue.text: 5 down in mulled ale going on and on

indicators.note: in puts the bird inside the jumbled letters
mulled wine is spiced and heated, so the letters of ale are stirred about

parts.note: 5 down is seabird, and a tern is a seabird

explanation.surface: A gull drowning in hot spiced beer seems to last forever.
explanation.walkthrough: '5 down' points to SEABIRD; the tern is one such bird, and 'mulled' suggests hot spiced drink but signals the shuffle.
explanation.definitionFit: Eternal describes something without end, so going on and on is a fair paraphrase.

clue.text: City of 5 down when inverted

indicators.note: when inverted means the two halves of 5 down swap places, the bird first

parts.note: 5 down is seabird, whose bird is here a swan
the first half of seabird gives sea

explanation.surface: A coastal city named for a seabird turned upside down.
explanation.walkthrough: 5 down is SEABIRD; read as SEA + a bird, SWAN, and swap the two parts to get the Welsh city.
explanation.definitionFit: Swansea is a coastal city in South Wales, the country's second largest.

clue.text: Boozer grabbing soft hat

indicators.note: grabbing means holding, so the boozer's letters enclose the next piece

parts.note: a toper is a heavy drinker
p is piano, soft in musical notation

explanation.surface: A drunk snatches a floppy hat.
explanation.definitionFit: A topper is an informal word for a top hat, the tall silk headgear.

clue.text: 5 down takes note: Billy was on track

parts.note: 5 down is seabird, and a puffin is a seabird
G is a musical note

explanation.surface: A seabird takes a note, while a goat called Billy trots along.
explanation.walkthrough: Puffing Billy was one of the earliest steam locomotives, built in 1813, so the 'Billy' on track was a puffing one.
explanation.definitionFit: The pioneer locomotive was named Puffing Billy, so the word completes the engine running on rails.

clue.text: Underline changes in an adult university etcetera etcetera

indicators.note: changes means alters, so the pieces that follow are rearranged

parts.note: A is the film certificate for adult
the second etcetera gives etc. again
the second etcetera gives etc. again

explanation.surface: Emphasise the changes in a grown-up college, and so on and so on.
explanation.definitionFit: To accentuate is to emphasise, which underlining a word does in writing.

clue.text: Politician leaves first part of 12 club

indicators.note: leaves means departs, so the politician is taken out

parts.note: 12 is chickenpox; its first part is chicken, a coward, which is a poltroon
pol is short for politician

explanation.surface: A politician leaves the opening of a disease report at a club.
explanation.walkthrough: 12 across is CHICKENPOX; its first part, CHICKEN, means a coward, POLTROON. Royal Troon is a championship golf club in Ayrshire, Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: Royal Troon is a famous Open Championship golf club on the Ayrshire coast.

clue.text: Sell club game back

indicators.note: back means going backwards, so the word for the game is read in reverse

parts.note: golf is the game played with clubs

explanation.surface: Selling off a golfer's club after the game.
explanation.definitionFit: Flog is British slang meaning sell, especially to sell something off cheaply.

clue.text: Building for insectivorous cat

annotationWithheld.why: Building for insectivorous cat (4-2): LEANTO is LEO (cat) with ANT inside, but 'insectivorous' both supplies ANT and signals the insertion, one word doing two jobs

clue.text: Southern Railway carrying veteran warriors

indicators.note: carrying means holding within, so the veteran goes inside

parts.note: an oldie is an old-timer, a veteran

explanation.surface: Old soldiers ride the Southern Railway.
explanation.definitionFit: Soldiery is a collective noun for soldiers, a body of fighting men.

clue.text: Fast woman as leader in state capital

indicators.note: in places the leader inside the city

parts.note: Atlanta is the capital of the US state of Georgia

indicators.note: leader means the first letter of the next word

explanation.surface: A racy woman takes the lead in a US state capital.
explanation.walkthrough: In Greek myth Atalanta was a swift runner who would marry only a man who outran her.
explanation.definitionFit: The mythical huntress was renowned for her speed, losing a race only to golden apples.
